ISSUE32_TECHNOLOGY_REVISION.DECISION: Use native net/http for the sole unversioned /conversations HTTP resource tree. Retain /ws as a separate WebSocket endpoint; it is not a conversation HTTP resource route. Do not add an external version router, rewriting facade, duplicated handler stack, /v1 or /v2 HTTP API.

Reuse existing BFE Drive Internal Auth UDS validation and session-bound DPoP proof/request binding for protected HTTP requests and /ws connections; do not introduce plain Bearer fallback. Authenticate the WebSocket connection and independently authorize every subscription against current conversation membership and visibility. Established subscriptions must stop protected delivery when membership is removed or access is revoked. Centrifuge does not replace application-level authorization.

Reuse the existing functional /v2 domain implementation as a source-code reuse baseline only after downstream GRACE approval; expose only the approved /conversations HTTP tree in the target. Reusing domain logic does not retain /v2 routes, a legacy compatibility layer, old-client support, or a production migration path.

Use Goose to define a clean target-only migration chain for fresh PostgreSQL 18.4 bootstrap. The final target contains only the active Issue #32 conversation schema and migration definitions required by that target; obsolete legacy schema/tables, SQL functions, legacy-only packages, and compatibility paths are not retained. Successful validation of the five currently existing migrations on PostgreSQL 18.4 proves compatibility of that existing set only and does not require all five files or their legacy definitions to remain in the final target-only chain. No legacy-data migration, old-client support, or compatibility-driven preservation of obsolete migration definitions is required. This Technology proposal does not authorize running migrations or changing any database.

ISSUE36_TECHNOLOGY_REVISION.SCOPE: Proposed Technology revision for the human-approved ISSUE36-REALTIME-REPLACEMENT requirements. It replaces Centrifuge with ntfy and UnifiedPush as the sole realtime push path. It does not authorize implementation, dependency edits, client changes, tests, deployment, infrastructure changes, or downstream GRACE artifacts. ISSUE36_TECHNOLOGY_REVISION.DECISION: Use a self-hosted ntfy server v2.34.0 as the only realtime push server and the ntfy Android application v1.25.2 as the initial UnifiedPush distributor. The Android BFE Chat application integrates the official UnifiedPush connector, receives the push in its own process, and creates the Android system notification itself. ntfy is not used as a second notification UI. Remove Centrifuge from the active target; do not retain WebSocket/Centrifuge delivery, a fallback transport, a parallel transport, or a compatibility path.

Use the UnifiedPush registration endpoint with its p256dh public key and auth secret as a Web Push subscription. Encrypt each payload according to RFC 8291 using the required aes128gcm content encoding and authenticate application-server requests with VAPID according to RFC 8292. Use the proposed webpush-go v1.4.0 library for the server-side protocol rather than implementing encryption or VAPID signing manually. Validate interoperability against ntfy v2.34.0 before production implementation is accepted; documentation review is not runtime compatibility evidence.

The decrypted application payload contains exactly the protocol version and opaque wakeToken. It must not contain message text, conversation/account identifiers, document ID/title/content, sender identity, or any other identifying metadata. Do not use ntfy title/body/click URL fields to expose conversation details. BFE Chat displays a generic system notification and keeps the wakeToken only in the notification's internal navigation state.

Generate wakeToken using a cryptographically secure random source and maintain a durable server-side mapping from the token to its conversation. Reuse the token for notifications associated with that conversation; resolving it is repeatable and does not consume or rotate it. Do not assign a fixed TTL or delete mappings by age: the server cannot know whether a delivered Android notification is still queued or can still be activated. The token is a reference only, never a credential or authorization grant. Every resolution revalidates the DPoP-bound session, current Chat availability, membership, and message visibility before returning conversation information.

Store each device's UnifiedPush endpoint, public encryption key, authentication secret, and owning account/device association as protected subscription data. Registration, replacement, and removal use the authenticated Chat API and existing DPoP-bound session; the concrete routes and request/response schemas belong to downstream GRACE contracts. A subscription identifies a delivery destination only and grants no access to conversations or history. Never return another account's registration data or write endpoint URLs, authentication secrets, wakeToken values, or full push payloads to logs.

Treat each push endpoint as a bearer capability. Require HTTPS and an exact origin match against the server-side configured allowlist; the initial allowlist contains the configured ntfy server origin. Reject arbitrary client-supplied hosts, redirects, invalid schemes, and endpoints outside the allowlist to prevent SSRF. Revalidate the endpoint and DNS/IP policy before each outbound request. Additional UnifiedPush distributors require explicit operator allowlisting; no endpoint supplied by a client can expand the allowlist.

Run ntfy as a private self-hosted instance over HTTPS with auth-default-access deny-all. Use random high-entropy UnifiedPush topics/endpoints that contain no account or conversation identifiers. Grant only the minimum write/read permissions required for the application-server publisher and registered ntfy distributor subscriptions; prefer per-topic ACLs where supported. Do not grant general public read/write access or expose administrative credentials to BFE Chat. Topic/endpoint secrecy is defense in depth, not Chat authorization; encrypted push payloads and the protected wakeToken-resolution API remain mandatory.

On receipt, BFE Chat creates a generic Android system notification with an internal intent containing only wakeToken and protocol version. Tapping it calls the protected Chat API to resolve wakeToken; only a successful current authorization check permits navigation to the conversation and authenticated history retrieval. Invalid, stale, revoked, or disabled-state tokens fail closed without revealing conversation identity or message content.

When Chat is administratively disabled, deny new Chat operations, history requests, wakeToken resolution, and new UnifiedPush registrations. An already-active ntfy subscription may continue delivering only the opaque wake payload; receiving it does not authorize any API request. After re-enable, authorized clients catch up through the existing history API. Do not introduce session revocation, periodic Drive-session checks, or a fixed delivery-stop deadline.

Commit the message before attempting ntfy delivery. A delivery failure never rolls back a persisted message; record the failure without logging secrets, and rely on authenticated history for recovery of missed messages. An idempotent message replay must not create a new logical notification. Do not add a separate durable notification queue/outbox in this Technology revision; any retry policy and its duplicate-delivery semantics must be specified by downstream contracts before implementation.

Retain PostgreSQL 18.4, pgx, Goose, native net/http, and the existing BFE Drive Internal Auth UDS/DPoP contract. Realtime events are hints only; persisted conversation history remains authoritative for catch-up, ordering, visibility, and read state. No API versioning, data migration, or legacy-client support is introduced by this technology choice.
